commands.name: list-sources

commands.name: report
commands.summary: Generate a human-readable backlog report on disk.

commands.summary: Show one or more full task cards by item key.

commands.name: search
commands.summary: Search tasks when keys are not yet known.

commands.name: gaps
commands.summary: List explicit blockers and unresolved gaps.

commands.name: queue

commands.name: delete-backlog
commands.summary: Delete the backlog and its utility-owned artifacts.

notes: Most commands are backlog-scoped and auto-discover `.backlog.json` from the current working directory or its parent directories.
For one backlog root, run mutating commands strictly one at a time.
Help shows strictly validated values and command semantics that change the mental model; use the reference docs for full field-level contracts.

register-source.summary: Register a source document and obtain a source ID.

options.description: Path to the source document to register.
Source kind defined by the skill contract.
Source authority defined by the skill contract.
Readable operator note attached to the source registration.

notes: This mutating command is backlog-scoped: run it from a backlog root or one of its child directories discovered through `.backlog.json`.
`--path` resolves from the current working directory, then the registered path is normalized relative to backlog root and may contain `..` for external sources.
For one backlog root, run mutating commands strictly one at a time.
Machine-facing filesystem paths in command output are absolute.

options.description: Output path for the generated template file.
Required for patch templates; comma-separated target item keys.

notes: `template packet` writes a draft skeleton and does not require an existing backlog root.
`template patch` is backlog-scoped: run it from a backlog root or one of its child directories discovered through `.backlog.json`.
`--out` resolves from the current working directory.
Machine-facing filesystem paths in command output are absolute.

packet.summary: Apply a packet that adds new backlog tasks.

options.description: Path to the authored packet file.
Validate and simulate packet application without writing to disk.

notes: This mutating command is backlog-scoped: run it from a backlog root or one of its child directories discovered through `.backlog.json`.
`--path` resolves from the current working directory.
`--dry-run` validates and simulates packet apply without writing canonical imports or backlog state.
On real apply, output distinguishes the authored draft from the immutable canonical import copy.
For one backlog root, run mutating commands strictly one at a time.
Machine-facing filesystem paths in command output are absolute.

options.description: Run refresh before returning the status summary.

notes: This command is backlog-scoped: run it from a backlog root or one of its child directories discovered through `.backlog.json`.
`status` returns a short summary of the current backlog state.
`status --refresh` first runs refresh, so treat it as a mutating composite command.
For one backlog root, run mutating commands strictly one at a time.

report.summary: Generate a human-readable backlog report on disk.
notes: This mutating command is backlog-scoped: run it from a backlog root or one of its child directories discovered through `.backlog.json`.
Report files are always written into the standard reports directory inside the backlog root.
For one backlog root, run mutating commands strictly one at a time.
Machine-facing filesystem paths in command output are absolute.

queue.summary: Return ordered chains of tasks that can be taken next.
notes: This command is backlog-scoped: run it from a backlog root or one of its child directories discovered through `.backlog.json`.
`queue` returns ordered ready chains, not a flat list of every ready item.
If `queue` is empty, inspect `gaps` and `attention` before assuming backlog creation failed.

gaps.summary: List explicit blockers and unresolved gaps.

options.description: Restrict output to a single task key.

notes: This command is backlog-scoped: run it from a backlog root or one of its child directories discovered through `.backlog.json`.
`--item-key` narrows the result to one task.
Empty output means there are no explicit blockers in the selected scope.

attention.summary: Return tasks that require review or re-checking.
notes: This command is backlog-scoped: run it from a backlog root or one of its child directories discovered through `.backlog.json`.
`attention` returns review and re-check items, not every blocked task in the backlog.
Entries are ordered by severity first, then by item key.
